short: Light-Assisted Rechargeable Lithium Batteries: Organic Molec
title: Light-Assisted Rechargeable Lithium Batteries: Organic Molecules for Simultaneous Energy Harvesting and Storage

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Photo-rechargeable batteries pairing separate light-harvesting and storage materials lose efficiency to charge transfer across their interface. One redox-active organic molecule that both absorbs light and stores Li should let light drive delithiation and assist charging.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/architecture), n5 (PRC/deposition), n6 (PRC/deposition), n7 (PRC/stimulus). Premises: Lawsone-based materials are semiconductors (band gap 3.81 eV) used as DSSC dyes; Own earlier work: bislawsone gave 125 mAh/g; the lawsone tetramer 227 mAh/g at 25 mA/g with better cycling

states.title: Structure state
states.head: CVD carbon coat covers the SS mesh wire surface uniformly. Discharge binds Li at TKL oxygen sites forming LiTKL; charging removes it back to TKL

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: TKL and Li-TKL both absorb visible light (optical gaps 2.67 and 2.41 eV). TKL LUMO (-3.7 eV) lies above the collector level (-4.3 eV), so photoexcited electrons can pass to the collector.
states.detail: Absorbed: n11 (PRP/value), n12 (PRP/descriptor), n12b (PRP/descriptor), n13 (MEC/pathway), n16 (MEC/pathway)

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Light accelerates charging: charging current at 3 V rises reversibly under irradiation. Discharging under light gives extra capacity: ~332 mAh/g vs ~296 in the preceding dark cycle.

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: A single henna-derived organic molecule (TKL) both harvests visible light and stores Li, and light accelerates its charging in a Li battery

nodes.title: evidence, F6
nodes.head: Within each light window the current ramps up over ~50-60 s and relaxes over tens of seconds after switch-off, not a prompt step
nodes.solves: Light makes electron-hole pairs in TKL; electrons flow via the carbon-coated mesh to the anode while holes oxidize LiTKL to TKL, releasing Li+
nodes.note: slow rise/decay is also what laser heating of the cell would give; no thermal or dark-heated control in the packet
nodes.detail: o15: Within each light window the current ramps up over ~50-60 s and relaxes over tens of seconds after switch-off, not a prompt step
nodes.inner_audit: o15: slow rise/decay is also what laser heating of the cell would give; no thermal or dark-heated control in the packet
